clip.tooltip: The CLIP model used for encoding the text.

ckpt_name.tooltip: The name of the checkpoint (model) to load.

images.tooltip: The images to create a video from.

audio.tooltip: The audio to add to the video.

bit_depth.tooltip: Auto uses 8-bit for sRGB and 10-bit for HDR. Explicit 8-bit and 10-bit choices are independent of colorspace.

color_space.tooltip: Colorspace of the input images. HDR selects BT.2020/HLG and HDR PQ selects BT.2020/PQ.

codec.tooltip: Optionally encode the video immediately. None keeps the images in tensor form; Auto uses H.264.

frames.tooltip: Input video frames. Feed the same frames you send to the depth node.

azimuth.tooltip: Horizontal orbit angle (deg). Negative orbits LEFT, positive RIGHT. The strongest control: +-45 is where the model has been checked, and the training set covers out to +-90 evenly. Past 90 the hidden side is invented.

elevation.tooltip: Vertical orbit angle (deg). Positive rises above the subject, negative looks up from below. UP is the weak direction: only 3.1% of the training set sits below -20.

distance.tooltip: Camera distance (1.0 = same as the source). Below 1 moves closer, above 1 pulls back - and pulling back reveals area the source never framed, so the magenta holes grow. The current LoRA does not follow this reliably.

hfov.tooltip: Assumed horizontal field of view (deg). ~50 is a normal lens; change it if the clip is clearly wide-angle or telephoto. 0 takes it from moge_geometry, which runs about 10% short - set it yourself if you know the lens.

vertical_shift.tooltip: Vertical lens shift, as a fraction of image height. Positive moves the picture DOWN, i.e. the framing up, which rescues a clipped head. The camera does not move, so parallax is unchanged. Leave at 0 unless the framing needs it.

depth_ratio.tooltip: Max far/near depth ratio of the scene. Lower = flatter relief and a cleaner warp; higher = more parallax but messier on cluttered scenes. Close-up faces: 2.5-4; mid shots: 4-8; deep/wide scenes: 8-16.

smooth_depth.tooltip: Edge-aware depth smoothing before warping. Turn ON if the warp has too many speckle holes; it trades a little sharpness for cleaner disocclusion.

invert_depth.tooltip: Flip depth polarity (near<->far). Leave OFF for the standard DA-V2 node. Turn ON only if the warp looks inside-out - background moving like foreground, or the subject caving in.

roll_lock.tooltip: Retired and ignored. It rolled the camera to hold the subject's projected lean, but the orbit introduces no roll to correct - a level source gives a level target at every angle - and what it was reacting to is keystone from elevation, which a roll cannot fix. Both training datasets have exactly 0 camera roll.

pivot_override.tooltip: Orbit around the explicit pivot below instead of an auto- estimated one. ON by default, which is the recommended setup.

pivot_x.tooltip: Pivot X in the source camera frame (+ = right), in depth units. 0 = image centre. The camera aims at the pivot, so moving this also reframes the shot - unless keep_source_aim is ON, where it only moves the orbit centre.

pivot_y.tooltip: Pivot Y (+ = down), in depth units. 0 = image centre. Doubles as a reframe like pivot_x. Use vertical_shift to reframe without moving the camera.

pivot_z.tooltip: Pivot depth. ~1.05 sits on the nearest subject in the middle of the frame; raise it to orbit something further back. The orbit radius is distance * |pivot|, so this widens the arc as well as moving its centre.

use_keyframes.tooltip: Animate the camera along the keyframes path instead of holding one pose. Switched on for you when the first keyframe is placed.

frame_count.tooltip: Retired and ignored. The clip length comes from the cached preview.

keyframes.tooltip: Camera path as JSON - normally written for you by the KEY button on the preview, or by right-clicking the orbit sphere. Each entry: 'f' is the frame number counted from 1, 'az'/'el' are degrees, 'dist' is the distance. Optional 'vs' (vertical shift) and 'px'/'py'/'pz' (the pivot) inherit the static widgets when left out; px/py/pz need pivot_override ON. Example: [{"f":1,"az":-30,"el":20,"dist":1.0},{"f":49,"az":45,"el":10,"dist":1.2}] . The pose is held before the first and after the last keyframe, so a path may cover only part of the clip. Empty = no move.

interp_motion.tooltip: Shape and timing of the camera path. linear = straight legs at constant speed. ease_in / ease_out / ease_in_out = the same legs with the camera settling into every keyframe. smooth = a Catmull-Rom spline gliding through them with no corner. Only used while use_keyframes is ON.

keep_source_aim.tooltip: Which point the orbiting camera looks at. OFF: it looks at the pivot, so the pivot sits dead centre and moving it reframes the shot. ON: it looks where the SOURCE camera looked, so your original framing is kept and the pivot is only the orbit centre. Needs pivot_x or pivot_y off zero to do anything - on the optical axis both aims are the same point. ON is what the training data does and scores 28.9 against 42.3 measured on the training warps; OFF by default for compatibility, turn it ON for new work.

depth.tooltip: Depth map for the same frames, from a Depth Anything V2 node. Brightness = depth; polarity is handled by invert_depth. Leave unconnected if you are feeding moge_geometry instead.

moge_geometry.tooltip: Metric geometry from Run MoGe Inference, used instead of the depth image. Depth then arrives in real metres, so depth_ratio, invert_depth and smooth_depth no longer apply, and pivot and distance become real distances. Measured against ground truth it roughly halves the warp error. hfov comes from its intrinsics when hfov is 0.

camera_info.tooltip: Exact target camera, from Create Camera Info or a Load 3D viewport. When connected the pose comes from it, and the orbit controls - angles, distance, hfov, the pivot and the keyframe path - are all ignored.

preview_size.tooltip: Longest side the clip is cached at for the live preview. The warp is scale-invariant, so this trades sharpness and memory for frame rate: about 1 MB per frame and 18 fps at 384, 1.8 MB and 11 fps at 512. Takes effect on the next run.

frame_index.tooltip: Playhead for the live preview, counted from 1. The scrub bar under the preview drives it; it does not affect the output and needs no re-run.

video.tooltip: The video to extract components from.

model.tooltip: The model used for denoising the input latent.

seed.tooltip: The random seed used for creating the noise.

steps.tooltip: The number of steps used in the denoising process.

cfg.tooltip: The Classifier-Free Guidance scale balances creativity and adherence to the prompt. Higher values result in images more closely matching the prompt however too high values will negatively impact quality.

sampler_name.tooltip: The algorithm used when sampling, this can affect the quality, speed, and style of the generated output.

scheduler.tooltip: The scheduler controls how noise is gradually removed to form the image.

positive.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to include in the image.

negative.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to exclude from the image.

denoise.tooltip: The amount of denoising applied, lower values will maintain the structure of the initial image allowing for image to image sampling.

image.tooltip: Image or video to condition the latent video on. Must be 8*n + 1 frames. If the video is not 8*n + 1 frames, it will be cropped to the nearest 8*n + 1 frames.

frame_idx.tooltip: Frame index to start the conditioning at. For single-frame images or videos with 1-8 frames, any frame_idx value is acceptable. For videos with 9+ frames, frame_idx must be divisible by 8, otherwise it will be rounded down to the nearest multiple of 8. Negative values are counted from the end of the video.

attention_mask.tooltip: Optional pixel-space spatial mask. Controls per-region conditioning influence via self-attention, multiplied by strength.

iclora_parameters.tooltip: Optional IC-LoRA parameters from a Get IC-LoRA Parameters node. Used for adjusting guide processing as required by certain IC-LoRAs (eg. those with a reference_downscale_factor > 1). When chained, each LTXVAddGuide uses only the parameters connected to it.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model used for decoding the latent.

batch_size.tooltip: The number of latent audio samples in the batch.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model to get configuration from.

img_compression.tooltip: Amount of compression to apply on image.

stretch.tooltip: Stretch the sigmas to be in the range [terminal, 1].

terminal.tooltip: The terminal value of the sigmas after stretching.

frame_idx.tooltip: Frame index to anchor the image or the clip's first frame at. Negative values are counted from the end of the video.

vae.tooltip: Video VAE, needed when an image is connected.

audio_vae.tooltip: Audio VAE, needed when an audio is connected.

image.tooltip: Image or video frames to anchor. Multi-frame batches are anchored as a clip and cropped down to the model's valid clip lengths: 5, 22, 39... (17k + 5) frames. Batches shorter than 5 frames use only the first image.

audio.tooltip: Soundtrack to anchor starting at the same frame index, cropped to the video's remaining duration.

length.tooltip: Frame count at 24 fps, snapped up to the model's 17k+5 grid (124 = ~5s; trained range is ~124-362, longer is untested)
Frame count at 24 fps, (124 = ~5s, trained range is ~124-362)

ref_image_size.tooltip: Reference image sizing. 'match' scales each ref (down only, keeping aspect) to the generation's pixel area; 'max' uses the reference pipeline's 2048px short edge for best identity fidelity. Reference tokens ride through every sampling step, so 'max' can be several times slower.

vae.tooltip: Video VAE. Without it reference images/videos only condition the text encoder.

audio_vae.tooltip: Audio VAE. Without it reference audio only conditions the text encoder.

ref_image.tooltip: Reference image (downscaled to 2048 short edge if larger, never upscaled)

ref_video_audio.tooltip: Soundtrack of the same-numbered reference video

fov_x_degrees.tooltip: Horizontal field of view of the source camera. Sets the focal length used to unproject the depth map into 3D. 0 = auto-recover from the predicted points.

batch_size.tooltip: Images per inference call. Lower if you OOM on a long video / image set.

apply_mask.tooltip: Set masked-out (sky / invalid) pixels to inf in points and depth so meshing culls them. Disable to keep the raw predicted geometry everywhere; the mask is still returned separately.

refine_steps.tooltip: MoGe-3 only: sparse volumetric refinement passes over the predicted depth. More passes sharpen fine detail and edges at a roughly linear cost. 0 disables refinement. Ignored by MoGe-1 / MoGe-2.

attention.tooltip: The dense attention backend. Comfy Kitchen attention uses quantized INT8 attention and is available only on Nvidia and AMD GPUs.

resize_type.tooltip: Select how to resize: by exact dimensions, scale factor, matching another image, etc.

width.tooltip: Target width in pixels. Set to 0 to auto-calculate from height while preserving aspect ratio.

height.tooltip: Target height in pixels. Set to 0 to auto-calculate from width while preserving aspect ratio.

crop.tooltip: How to handle aspect ratio mismatch: 'disabled' stretches to fit, 'center' crops to maintain aspect ratio.

multiplier.tooltip: Scale factor (e.g., 2.0 doubles size, 0.5 halves size).

longer_size.tooltip: The longer edge will be resized to this value. Aspect ratio is preserved.

shorter_size.tooltip: The shorter edge will be resized to this value. Aspect ratio is preserved.

width.tooltip: Target width in pixels. Height auto-adjusts to preserve aspect ratio.

height.tooltip: Target height in pixels. Width auto-adjusts to preserve aspect ratio.

megapixels.tooltip: Target total megapixels (e.g., 1.0 ≈ 1024×1024). Aspect ratio is preserved.

match.tooltip: Resize input to match the dimensions of this reference image or mask.

crop.tooltip: How to handle aspect ratio mismatch: 'disabled' stretches to fit, 'center' crops to maintain aspect ratio.

multiple.tooltip: Resize so width and height are divisible by this number. Useful for latent alignment (e.g., 8 or 64).

scale_method.tooltip: Interpolation algorithm. 'area' is best for downscaling, 'lanczos' for upscaling, 'nearest-exact' for pixel art.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: The aspect ratio for the output dimensions.

megapixels.tooltip: Target total megapixels. 1.0 MP ≈ 1024x1024 for square.

multiple.tooltip: Nearest multiple of the result to set the selected resolution to.

preview.tooltip: Live preview of the calculated output resolution.

filename_prefix.tooltip: The prefix for the file to save. This may include formatting information such as %date:yyyy-MM-dd% or %Empty Latent Image.width% to include values from nodes.

format.tooltip: The output container. Auto uses MP4 for Auto/H.264 and WebM for AV1. MP4, MKV, and WebM select a specific container.

codec.tooltip: The output video codec. Auto preserves a compatible source stream. H.264 and AV1 re-encoding support SDR, HDR (HLG), and HDR PQ.

encoding.tooltip: Automatic preserves compatible H.264 streams. Re-encode applies custom encoding options.

crf.tooltip: Lower values produce higher quality and larger files.

encoding.tooltip: Automatic preserves compatible AV1 streams. Re-encode applies custom encoding options.
